lesson_title: Every Tool in Your Drawer Is Two Levers
hook_text: Scissors, pliers, nutcracker, stapler, tweezers. Each one is a pair of levers, and each pair is a different class.
clip_script: Tip the kitchen drawer onto the table. Scissors and pliers: the pivot screw sits between your hand and the jaws. First class. Cut near the screw, easy; cut at the tips, hard. Nutcracker and office punch: the hinge is at the end, the nut or paper sits right beside it, your hand is far away. Load in the middle, second class, and a walnut near the hinge gives up instantly. Stapler and tweezers: hinge at the back, fingers in the middle, tips at the front. Effort in the middle, third class. You squeeze harder than the tips push, but the tips move further, so you can pick up a splinter without crushing it. Now chain levers together with several pivots and you get a linkage: a folding clothes airer that stretches, a car jack that lifts a tonne, and the Jaws of Life, where a piston pushes two first-class arms and the tips spread a car door. Your rescue jaws will be exactly that linkage, in cardboard.
visual_style: Whiteboard tools laid out in three rows with the pivot circled on each; then crossed bars of an airer extending and two spreader arms closing on a pin.
mood: Hands-on and inquisitive, like sorting treasure from a drawer.
pacing: Three tool pairs in quick succession, then a slower zoom into linkages and the spreader.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the two-strip card mock-up of your rescue jaws.
